title: Customary patient counseling before an administered dose
rule_summary: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124 provides that a pharmacist or pharmacy intern must provide customary patient counseling prior to administering a dose of an approved medication. Such counseling may include information about common side-effects, drug interactions, dietary requirements, injection site reaction and other information routinely provided to patients upon dispensing, as appropriate within the professional judgment of the pharmacist and in accordance with 247 CMR 2.00 et seq.
exam_relevance: Tests that counseling is required before administering a dose of an approved medication while its content is framed as what may be included, as appropriate within the pharmacist's professional judgment.

authority.name: Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, March 11, 2026

common_confusions: Treating the listed counseling topics as a mandatory script, when the circular says counseling may include them as appropriate within the pharmacist's professional judgment.
Treating counseling as optional because its content is discretionary, when the circular says the pharmacist or intern must provide customary patient counseling prior to administering a dose.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-14 in Circular Letter DCP 26-03-124, Pharmacist Administration of Medications, dated March 11, 2026, in the Word document linked from the Department's news page on mass.gov.
